newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr down vs yen in Tokyo on trade issue caution.
newsitem.headline: Dlr down vs yen in Tokyo on trade issue caution.

text.p: 0629 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar slid against the yen by late Tokyo on Thursday, with its topside heavy as the market became cautious about U.S.-Japan trade relations, dealers said.

The dollar dipped below 118 yen on long liquidation sales in late Tokyo, depressed by comments by a senior official of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA), but traders said the dollar's undertone remains bullish.
Takao Tominaga, vice chairman and executive managing director of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA), said he does not want to see the dollar strengthening from the current level.
Traders took his comments as a good excuse to unload dollar-long positions, but they said his comments alone would not change the recent uptrend of the dollar.

"Usually, comments from vice chairman (of JAMA) would not have an impact, but the market took them as a trading factor because it has become sensitive (towards trade issues) after overnight rumours," a dealer at a long-term credit bank said.
In New York on Wednesday, traders cited rumours that U.S. car makers wanted Washington to review U.S.-Japan trade barriers, which dragged the greenback from a high 118.95 yen.
In early Tokyo trade, the dollar fell below 118 yen on active selling from U.S. operators and stop-loss sales triggered near 118.10 and 117.90 yen.

But it soon recovered due to purchases by Japanese investors, such as life insurers and trust banks, dealers said. "Even if the dollar is pushed down on trade issues, basically its downside is solid. So after traders confirm that the greenback will test 119 yen again," a city bank dealer said.

Dealers said the underlying sentiment towards the dollar is still bullish amid a growing perception that Japan's interest rates will remain low after the weak industrial output data for Japan released on Thursday. "After seeing the output data, I think it is not wise to hold yen," a U.S. bank dealer said.
The market now awaits the release of U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data for the second quarter at 1230 GMT and job data due out on Friday.
Wall Street pundits expect GDP to have expanded by 1.9 percent in the second quarter of the year against 5.9 percent growth in the first quarter.
The dollar remained on firm ground against the mark on Thursday, but fresh gains were expected to be blocked by growing expectations of a German interest rate hike, Singapore dealers said.

In other trade, sterling, seen as a high-yielding currency, edged up against the dollar on short-covering and purchases by Japanese investors, dealers said. It was quoted at $1.6415/20 at 0715 GMT, up sharply from $1.6280/90 in late New York on Wednesday. The dollar closed at 118.40/45 yen and 1.8360/70 marks in New York on Wednesday. -- Sonali Desai, Singapore newsroom +65-8703090, Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8584
